plaintext.source: The volume's own clear copy: ff. 101r-155r give the text of ff. 3r-96v and ff. 166r-170r that of ff. 158r-162r, 'aber in normaler Schrift geschrieben' (Steinmann's unprinted description, PRIOR_ART.md). The volume also holds its key: f. 99r (Danish notes) with a German translation on f. 98r, viewed here only after the decode.

system.summary: A secret alphabet of invented and digit-like signs for Latin letters, with signs for common letter groups (et, er, es, it, st, ct, sc, nt, ae), a few word signs (qui, quod, quam, que, non), and marks on a sign that add m (dot above) or n (dot below) or double its letter (two dots above).

diacritics.note: A dot above a sign adds m and a dot below adds n after its letter; two dots above double the letter; two dots on the line repeat a vowel written earlier in the word (the key leaf: the letter before with a dot in its middle) and three dots a letter further back; a bar or a loop on a sign makes another sign (Bx~ non, Oe~, Tk@, Dl@).

system.notes: 51 base sign labels (SIGNS.md, the placeholder ? not counted) and 6 marks; the recovered key (KEY.tsv) values 62 tokens and two rules. Homophones counted from KEY.tsv: e has 6, D1 and Cd, s has 6s, 6v, Ph and Ar; several of these are word-final forms or context signs on the key leaf (Ea a, Lr t, Pl r and Ar s final; D1 e after r, i after t). The 7 word signs met in training are Oe" quod, Oe^m quam, Oei qui, Oe~ (quas or quae in training, quem on the leaf), Q3 que, Bx~ non and 5~ (igitur, no letters in the key); the key leaf lists more (quae, enim, autem) and calls them abbreviations as usual in Latin. Line fillers and line-end hyphens carry no value. The volume's own key leaf (f. 99r, Danish; German translation f. 98r) is the same key; it was compared only after the decode (work/keyleaf_vs_key.tsv).

prior_solution.where: In the volume itself: the clear copy (ff. 101r-155r, 166r-170r) and the key leaf f. 99r with its German translation f. 98r (Steinmann's description; swisscollections). Not opened: Skinner and Rankine 2008, Mathers 1889, Boudet's census of Clavicula manuscripts.

Run 2, the key of record: 301 word pairs, no cipher word unpaired, 62 tokens valued. Two context rules adopted on training counts (bar 70%): two dots on the line = the nearest preceding vowel of the word (34 of 43), two dots above = the letter twice (14 of 14). Ambiguous tokens take their majority value (Cl r 9 / i 6; Dl@ s 9 / us 8 / as 7). Key frozen at 12:55:46 UTC (FREEZE_KEY.txt).

outcome.notes: Held-out design: the key was built from ff. 4r-4v against the clear copy only; ff. 15r, 159r and 34r were decoded once with the frozen key, scored by a separate strict judge and, after the decode, against the clear copy. Blindness limits (FREEZE_TX.txt): the training leaves were transcribed with the clear copy beside them; the held-out leaves were transcribed by a reader who knew most of the system; the first two lines of H2's clear page were seen at contact-sheet size before the decode. The key leaf was viewed only after the key freeze and the decode (the contributor's record; the file times agree, and the RFC 3161 stamps of 21:21 UTC come after all of it). First pass: the decode puts 65.6% of letters in words that read as sense but builds no clean sentence, so each first-pass passage is 'decoded, not read' under README Conventions ('A reading must read'). The class is 'read in part' since 28 Nov 2026, at Dan Bourdeau's request (review of 27 Nov 2026 on PR #957): each pass-5 text takes its state from its own count; the reading review is left to the maintainers. Verification is of the key: the volume's clear copy (80.3% of its letters reproduced on the held-out passages) and its key leaf (46 of 52 values). The shuffle control and the judge are model work and are in the solution steps.
